source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
description: Banana leaf fig is an evergreen tree in the Moraceae (fig) family native to India, Southeast Asia and China. It is commonly grown as a houseplant in temperate climates. The most popular one found for sale is the cultivar 'Alii' which is sometimes sold with a braided trunk. In their native habitat, they grow quite large and produce small figs. As a house plant, they may reach 6- 10 feet tall. They can be pruned to control size if needed. These plants do best with bright indirect lighting. Plant in a potting mixture with good drainage and water the plant once the top 1-2 inches of the soil has dried out as they don't like soggy soils. They only need to be fertilized twice yearly. The stems contain latex which can cause contact dermatitis for some people so handle carefully when pruning. Insects, Diseases, and Other Plant Problems: whitefly, scale, and ficus mealybug can be a problem. cultivars.name: Alii
cultivars.note: 3 to 10 inches long, olive green, slender leaves with a drooping affect, easier to grow other varieties

cultivars.name: Alii Variegated
cultivars.note: chartreuse leaves with dark green speckles, young leaves are bronze

cultivars.name: Amstel King
cultivars.note: shiny, banana-shaped, dark green leaves, small weeping tree

Wildlife Value: In its native habitat, the fig wasp pollinates the flower inside the fruit. Birds and mammals will eat the fruits
Light: Dappled Sunlight (Shade through upper canopy all day)
Deep shade (Less than 2 hours to no direct sunlight)
Fruit Description: The small fruits develop in pairs at the leaf axils. They are yellow to red, with a flat or swollen opening at the bottom of the fruit when mature. It is best to remove the fruits when they appear
Flower Description: The tiny flowers develop within the fig.
Leaf Description: The stalked leathery leaves are spirally arranged and are oblong to oval to lance-shaped or slightly ovate and 3-10 by 1.5-3.5 inches.
